messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Custom claim-reference format missing",
 "problem_statement": "Users cannot define custom claim-reference formats to match internal naming conventions. This causes data mismatches during report generation and supplier syncing.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "We really need to set up a custom claim-reference format because our internal systems use specific naming conventions and we can’t have mismatches when pulling reports or syncing with suppliers.",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-10-12T08:59:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The single onboarding quote directly requests a custom claim-reference format to match internal naming conventions, describing data mismatches in reports and supplier syncing. This is a clear feature request and product gap a squad could act on, with no evidence the cause is pricing, contracts, or customer-side issues. The evidence is limited to one quote but it is unambiguous.", "verdict": "pass"}
